tools.name: analyze_accounts
tools.description:
Score accounts for evidence that more than one person is using them, and return the accounts they are behaviourally linked to.

Each account's sessions are clustered into 'cores' -- groups that look like a single person. Per account you get:
  p_shared        0..1, probability the account is used by several people
  verdict         'single' (p<0.5), 'review' (p<0.938), 'shared' (p>=0.938)
  session_groups  one array of session ids per person found
  links           up to 5 other accounts on the same platform whose behaviour matches, each with a 0..1 score

Every account costs a GPU draw, so pass them all in one call rather than looping one at a time.

To analyse ONE person inside a shared account, pass that person's ids from a previous session_groups result as session_ids (with exactly one account_id). The parent account is then excluded from that person's links, so what comes back is who that individual is linked to elsewhere.

account_ids.description: Account hashes to score. Batch them; do not loop.

session_ids.description: Optional. 32-char hex session ids selecting one person inside the account. Requires exactly one account_id.

include_coassignment.description: Also return the full N x N session co-assignment matrix. Grows with the square of the session count -- only ask for it on small accounts.

tools.name: top_shared_accounts
tools.description:
List your platform's accounts with the highest sharedness, most shared first.

Reads a live leaderboard: no GPU cost. An account appears only once it has been scored by analyze_accounts at least once, so this reflects what has been analysed so far, not the whole platform.

tools.name: top_linked_accounts
tools.description:
List the strongest behavioural links between pairs of accounts on your platform, strongest first. Useful for finding rings of accounts driven by one person.

Same live leaderboard as top_shared_accounts: no GPU cost, and it only covers accounts that have already been analysed.
